chapter_title: Concerning the Form of the Word, that [ ... 30 ...
spiritual_reading:
#
 Spiritual
 Translation


**
¶1:** The in
most will
 receives
 the influx of wisdom and draws
 it upward into
 awareness
. The understanding unfolds it
 and gives
 it bread
th and artic
ulation. The natural reasoning faculty
 discriminates it
,
 dividing it into distinct
 particulars. The outermost sens
ory faculty gathers these particul
ars into a coherent external form.
 Thus a spiritual truth proceeds
 out
ward through
 five
 successive degrees of the mind —
 from
 the in
most impul
se of
 the will to its
 final
 utter
ance — and becomes perceptible to
 those
 who stand
 in
 the external world.

**¶
2:** So
 it
 is with a
 formed doctrine: one faculty pours forth
 the raw substance of truth from the divine
 influx; another lab
ors upon
 it through sustained
 reflection; another trims away what is
 excessive or false as
 it is turned
 and
 examined
; another impresses upon it the authentic
 stamp
 of divine order; another purifies it
 through the sieve
 of discernment. These five interior
 faculties shape and perfect the doctrine until
 it enters the common
 life of
 the spiritual community. It becomes a living
 good
 that can be received into the understanding of
 one
 person
 and communicated to another through charity.


**¶3:** This
 is the
 nature
 of every
 truth that proceeds
 from the interior life: it is formed
 and made beautiful through
 the five degrees of the mind's operation
. It comes forth from the interior person
 and is received into the spiritual
 perception
 of others.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: [The word is formed by five members. The lung receives the air] and the throat draws it up and the tongue spreads it out and the teeth cut it and the lips g[at]her it! The word shall come forth through the power of th[ese five] members and be heard outside.
This is also the case with the [wor]d, as it is formed and embellished by five [member]s. It comes forth and is heard by the ears [of] others.

Simila[rly] the coin: One shall pour it out and an [othe]r beat it and another trim it as it is turned, and a[nother] put the stamp on it and another wipe it in the sieve (?). [Behold], these five craftsmen shall shape and beautify [their] coin, and it comes amongst mankind. It becomes a posse[ssion] to be received and given.

fills.fill: The word is formed by five members. The lung receives the air
